encounters.cc: Severe deep bone pain in extremities triggered by cold weather

lines: Severe deep bone pain in extremities triggered by cold weather

The patient is a 19-year-old male with HbSS sickle cell disease, functional asplenia, and avascular necrosis of the right femoral head who presents to the emergency department three months following his January 2020 hematology outpatient visit for routine follow-up.

He reports a history of recurrent painful episodes in his extremities, which he describes as "deep bone pain." He states that these episodes have been occurring since childhood and are often triggered by cold weather or dehydration.
- Avascular necrosis of right femoral head
- History of recurrent acute chest syndrome
His past medical history is significant for sickle cell anemia, and he has been hospitalized twice in the past year for acute chest syndrome.
- Penicillin VK 250 mg oral twice daily
Alcohol: Rare (special occasions only), avoids due to dehydration risk.

His oxygen saturation is 97% on room air.
On examination, he appears to be in mild distress.

encounters.cc: Persistent right groin pain with ambulation worsening over six months

lines: Persistent right groin pain with ambulation worsening over six months
This 20-year-old male with HbSS sickle cell anemia and right femoral head avascular necrosis returns for orthopedic follow-up after Hematology and ED encounters.
He presents with a 6-month history of persistent right groin pain, describing it as a dull ache worsening with walking and somewhat relieved by rest.
He denies any recent trauma, fever, or weight loss.
- Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Avascular necrosis of right femoral head
- History of recurrent acute chest syndrome
His past medical history is significant for sickle cell disease, for which he has been hospitalized twice in the past year for vaso-occlusive crises.
- Penicillin VK 250 mg oral twice daily
Alcohol: Rare (special occasions only), avoids due to dehydration risk.

Physical examination reveals a full range of motion in the right hip, but the patient reports pain with internal rotation.
There is no warmth, erythema, or swelling of the joint.
Radiographs of the right hip show irregularities in the femoral head's contour with subchondral sclerosis but no evidence of fracture or dislocation.

lines: Sudden severe left upper quadrant abdominal pain radiating to left shoulder
Patient with HbSS and functional asplenia presents with left upper quadrant pain.
He reports having had a sore throat, fever, and fatigue for the past week, which improved with rest and hydration.
He denies any recent trauma or injury.
- Sickle cell disease with vaso-occlusive crisis (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- Osteonecrosis of right femoral head (avascular necrosis) (diagnosed 2021-01-15)
- Avascular necrosis of right femoral head

Occupation: Part-time library assistant, community college student.
His vital signs are: blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, heart rate 120 beats per minute, respiratory rate 22 breaths per minute, and temperature 37.8°C (100°F).
On examination, he appears pale and diaphoretic.
Abdominal examination reveals tenderness in the left upper quadrant with guarding.
There is no rebound tenderness or rigidity.
An abdominal ultrasound shows an enlarged spleen with a hypoechoic area suggestive of a subcapsular hematoma.

lines: Worsening fatigue, jaundice, and dark urine following recent transfusion

He reports receiving a red blood cell transfusion 10 days ago due to a sickle cell crisis.
